title: Aoyagi Toya — Delicious Cultural Exposure〔Part1〕Side Story (Part 1)

rows.Line: Flea Market

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: They have more food trucks lined up over here.

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line:
Oh? Hey, they've got a big selection.
Birria, lobster rolls and... How do you read this? Souvlaki?

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: I've never heard of a lot of these foods before...

rows.Speaker: An
rows.Line: I can imagine what lobster rolls involve, but I honestly have no idea what birria and souvlaki are.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: They're not things you see very often in Japan.

rows.Speaker: Slade
rows.Line: Souvlaki's a type of meat that's grilled on a skewer. They serve it with this yogurt sauce called tzatziki.

rows.Speaker: An
rows.Line: Wait, yogurt sauce?

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: We grill all sorts of meat on skewers in Japan, but we usually use soy marinade and stuff...

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: I'm curious as to what it tastes like.

rows.Speaker: An
rows.Line: Then, what about birria?

rows.Speaker: Cedric
rows.Line: It's a type of stew that's made using chilis and herbs. People get hooked on the spiciness and flavor of the meat.

rows.Speaker: Slade
rows.Line: You eat it by dipping tortillas in it, and it's amazing! I bet you guys would love it!

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I see. That does sound good.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Since we're here, why don't we give it a try?

rows.Speaker: An
rows.Line: Yeah. A few other things caught my eye, but...

rows.Speaker: An
rows.Line: Huh...?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Is something wrong?

rows.Speaker: An
rows.Line: No, I just noticed that they're selling American dogs over there...

rows.Speaker: An
rows.Line: But they're calling them something else.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line:
You're right.
Let's see... It says “corn dogs”.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Yes, that's what they're called over here.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
It seems it's because they use cornmeal...
A flour made using crushed corn.

rows.Speaker: Slade
rows.Line: Hey, you know your stuff, Toya!

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I learned about it during one of my previous visits overseas.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line:
Corn flour...
Aren't they made using wheat flour in Japan?

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: So, these ones taste a bit different?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: That's certainly a possibility.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Still, it's interesting how the same food can be prepared differently depending on the country you're in.

rows.Speaker: An
rows.Line: We've been hit by surprises left and right since coming here! For example, the size of the hamburgers!

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Yes, and that also applies to music.

rows.Speaker: An
rows.Line: Oh, are you talking about the alleyway behind the academy?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: It was very similar to Vivid Street, but different types of music were being played there.

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: Yeah, everything from classical to pop.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: People were even playing traditional folk music. I'd never heard anyone put on that kind of street performance before.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Me neither. It's nice that we're getting to experience these differences in culture firsthand.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Even small discoveries, like the names of food, help us better ourselves and enrich our perspectives.

rows.Speaker: Cedric
rows.Line: Wow...

rows.Speaker: Cedric
rows.Line: That's an interesting way to approach visiting another country. It's actually kind of cool.

rows.Speaker: Slade
rows.Line: Didn't expect we'd hit on something so profound when this all started with corn dogs, though!

rows.Speaker: Slade
rows.Line: Or wait, is this one of those cultural differences too?

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: No, this is more Toya culture than Japanese culture...

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Hehe. He's just like that.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
Anyway, I digress...
Since we're here, why don't we have ourselves some corn dogs?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I believe tasting the difference for ourselves is the best solution.

rows.Speaker: An
rows.Line:
Oh, I'm in!
I really wanna have one now!

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Me too. I can't wait to see what they taste like.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Then, let's go buy some.
